name: Dientamoeba fragilis

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Trophozoite: approximately 5–15 µm, usually two nuclei, fragmented karyosomal chromatin and no peripheral nuclear chromatin.
One-nucleated forms occur; cyst-like forms are not the usual routine diagnostic target.

transmission.detail: Intestinal colonization and fecal shedding are established; transmission remains incompletely understood and should not be represented as a proven single route.

life_cycle.detail: Intestinal colonization and fecal shedding are established; transmission remains incompletely understood and should not be represented as a proven single route.

hosts: Humans are the main clinical host; animal findings exist. No established intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide; detection rates depend strongly on laboratory methods.
clinical_significance: Associated with gastrointestinal symptoms in some patients, but asymptomatic carriage occurs and causal interpretation needs context.
diagnostics: Permanent trichrome or iron-hematoxylin stains around 1000×; molecular assays improve detection.
Delayed fixation can degrade diagnostic nuclear features.
differential_diagnosis: Small amoebae and degenerating cells can resemble trophozoites; evaluate nuclei in well-preserved stained material.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Dientamoeba fragilis — Dientamoeba intestinal protist. Associated with gastrointestinal symptoms in some patients, but asymptomatic carriage occurs and causal interpretation needs context.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
